title: G006 checkpoint push strength sweep (evaluation only)
question: At what body-frame push magnitude does the G006 baseline policy leave the recovery-rate ceiling, and how do the existing baseline and push-curriculum checkpoints compare there?

scope.training: none; the six existing G006 model_1499 checkpoints are only evaluated
unchanged_from_g006: terrain, held-out rows/cols, initial states, commands, push directions, push timing
success_criteria, observation corruption off, evaluation domain randomization off
scripts/evaluate_push_recovery.py and src/isaac_walk_g006/evaluation (bundle sha256 must equal g006_queue_state.evaluation_source_bundle_sha256)
scope.guardrail_mode: not rerun; push magnitude does not enter no-push guardrail trials

runs.condition: only if every A1 magnitude has recovery_rate > ceiling_threshold

calibration.selection_rule: k = first ladder index whose calibration recovery_rate <= ceiling_threshold; comparison grid = three consecutive ladder values starting at max(0, min(k - 1, len(ladder) - 3)); if no index qualifies, stop with verdict no_knee_within_ladder and do not run phase B

comparison.primary_metric: push recovery rate over the 1080 grid trials, paired hierarchical bootstrap of push_curriculum minus baseline, 108 strata, 10000 draws, bootstrap seed 20260824
secondary: per-magnitude recovery rate with Wilson 95% interval, pooled and per seed
same paired delta restricted to seeds 43 and 44 because seed 42 baseline was used for calibration
tracking_error_sq, torque_l2, absolute_mechanical_power over post-push trials
comparison.ceiling_exit_confirmed_if: pooled three-seed baseline recovery rate at the knee magnitude (ladder[k]) is <= ceiling_threshold
comparison.difference_claim_rule: state a direction only if the primary 95% CI excludes 0; otherwise report no detectable difference

claim_boundary: Evaluation-only analysis of existing checkpoints; not the retrained step-2 comparison with five or more seeds.
Three training seeds per variant; seed 42 baseline also chose the grid.
A push is an instantaneous root velocity delta in simulation; magnitudes are not calibrated to any real robot or force.
Recovery after a push is not getting up from a fallen posture.
